title: VertiMRF: Differentially Private Vertical Federated Data Synthesis

problem.claim: Vertical federated data synthesis must preserve privacy while efficiently and precisely reconstructing correlations between attributes distributed across different data parties.

gap.claim: Existing data synthesis in this setting faces challenges because privacy protection can interfere with accurate reconstruction of cross-party attribute correlations, especially for attributes with large domains.

contributions.claim: VertiMRF is an algorithm for differentially private synthetic data generation in the vertical setting.
The method uses Flajolet-Martin sketches to encode local data under differential privacy and estimate cross-party marginals.
A central server reconstructs a global Markov Random Field from locally generated private MRFs and sketches, using dimension reduction and consistency enforcement to limit the impact of sketch noise.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present VertiMRF as a novel algorithm designed for differentially private synthetic data generation in the vertical setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world datasets.
The authors report that end-to-end comparisons demonstrate VertiMRF's superiority.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data synthesis can support downstream analytics without exposing raw data, but privacy guarantees are needed to prevent sensitive information leakage.
Vertical federated synthesis must protect privacy while reconstructing correlations across distributed attributes.
VertiMRF combines differentially private FM sketches, local private MRFs, and global MRF reconstruction.
Dimension reduction and consistency enforcement address sketch noise and permit flexible, inconsistent local binning while preserving information.
The method is evaluated on four real-world datasets through end-to-end comparisons.

source_observation.claim: The method combines local differential privacy, sketch-based marginal estimation, and server-side global MRF reconstruction.

interpretation.claim: Privacy-preserving synthesis can be organized as a pipeline that separates local encoding from global structure reconstruction.

application.claim: This pattern may be applicable when data holders cannot pool raw attributes but a coordinating server can aggregate privacy-protected summaries.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how this approach performs under privacy budgets, domain sizes, or party configurations not evaluated in the reported experiments.

unknowns: The privacy parameters and formal threat model are not specified.
The abstract does not identify the four datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The stated theoretical privacy and utility proofs are not detailed.
Reproducibility details and implementation availability are not provided.
